transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I know a few people in my department have quietly agreed to block my grants and promotions, and I can’t shake that belief no matter how much my wife or colleagues argue with me. It's why I'm here today, even though everyone else keeps telling me I'm just overthinking it.
Have you experienced any other beliefs that you know are not true but can't seem to shake, or is this feeling of being blocked at work the only one that's been bothering you?

Just to be clear, I don't think this is "not true"—I am absolutely certain that those people in my department are actively working against me. But yes, this situation at work is the only thing going on, and there aren't any other plots or beliefs bothering me.

Can you tell me more about when these beliefs about your coworkers blocking your grants and promotions started, and have they been persistent or have you had any periods where you didn't think about them?

This all started about a year ago, right after I lost out on a major research grant for the second time and a younger colleague got the faculty job instead of me. Since then, it has been completely constant, and there hasn't been a single period where I doubted what they were doing, despite my wife trying to convince me otherwise.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that others cannot, or have your beliefs about your coworkers been based solely on your interpretation of their actions and events?

No, I've never heard voices or seen things that aren't there. My understanding of the situation is based entirely on real, observable actions, like delayed emails, lukewarm feedback on my teaching, and sudden changes in meeting agendas. These are concrete events that clearly point to a coordinated effort to sideline me.
Have you taken any actions or made significant decisions based on your belief that your coworkers are blocking your grants and promotions, such as confronting them or changing your work habits?

Yes, I recently turned down a co-authorship offer because I was convinced it was a trap designed to discredit me. I've also started avoiding certain collaborators, skipping department socials, and spending my evenings tracking committee rosters for proof, though I still manage to get my basic teaching assistant duties done. It's just necessary precautions to protect myself from their coordination.
Have you experienced any significant distress or impairment in your social or occupational functioning as a result of these beliefs, beyond just taking precautions to protect yourself?

While I still manage to perform my basic teaching assistant duties and chores at home adequately, this situation has definitely strained my relationships. I've started skipping department socials, turning down collaboration opportunities, and spending my evenings obsessively tracking committee rosters instead of relaxing with my wife. It has created a lot of tension both at work and at home, even though my actual job performance is still fine.
Have you ever had a period where you were not preoccupied with the belief that your coworkers are plotting against you, or has this belief been continuously present over the past year?

Yes, it has been continuously present without any breaks at all over the past year. Ever since I missed out on that grant and my younger colleague got the position, this suspicion has been a constant presence in my mind. There hasn't been a single day where I felt free of this worry or doubted what they were doing.
Have you ever had any other persistent beliefs or fears that you think might be part of a larger pattern or conspiracy beyond just your coworkers blocking your grants and promotions?

No, there is absolutely no larger conspiracy or other fears going on. This is strictly a localized issue involving a specific group of people in my department who are targeting my career. I don't believe there is any broader pattern beyond their actions against me.

Have you considered the possibility that your beliefs about your coworkers might be an exaggeration or misinterpretation of their actual intentions, or do you still firmly believe that they are actively plotting against you?

My wife and others have told me I'm just overthinking or misinterpreting things, but I still firmly believe they are actively working against me. There are simply too many "coincidences"—like the delayed emails and sudden schedule changes—for it to be anything else. It is impossible for me to see it any other way.

Can you describe how your belief about your coworkers affects your daily life and relationships, and are there any times when you feel like this belief is not entirely true or when you have doubts about it?

My day-to-day teaching duties and household chores are still fine, but my relationships are strained because I'm skipping department socials and spending my evenings tracking committee rosters instead of relaxing with my wife. As for doubts, I have absolutely none; despite my wife and colleagues trying to convince me otherwise, I am completely certain this is real and I cannot shake the belief.

The patient's ability to maintain daily functioning, despite strained relationships and obsessive behaviors related to the belief, and the lack of other persistent beliefs or fears beyond the specific issue at hand, further supports F22 as the more likely candidate.
